rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun ‘before it’ most likely refers to the proof in the preceding verse, understood as the Qur’an; destroying them before its arrival would leave their case unanswered.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن ضمير { من قبله } للبينة - في الآية السابقة - باعتبار أنها القرآن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes ‘before it’ to refer to the messenger implied by the preceding verse; this is close verbally, but the Qur’an reading is stronger in meaning and fits ‘follow Your signs.’
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير للرسول المعلوم من مضمون الآية السابقة بشهادة قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarabbus means waiting, and the straight path is the upright road; each side waits for its desired outcome and follows a way toward it.
rows.anchor: التربص الانتظار، والصراط السوي الطريق المستقيم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers await God’s promised triumph, the advance of His religion, and the completion of His light; the opponents await reversals that would extinguish the true call.
rows.anchor: فنحن ننتظر ما وعده الله لنا فيكم وفي تقدم دينه وتمام نوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to wait is a threat: the parties will learn which follows the straight road to its goal and is guided; the verse foretells a victory.
rows.anchor: وفيه تهديد فستعلمون أي طائفة منا ومنكم أصحاب الطريق المستقيم

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi says the punishment would have befallen them, but God delayed it until an appointed term.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { لكان لزاما وأجل مسمى } قال كان ينزل بهم العذاب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet identifies the prayer before sunrise as the dawn prayer and the prayer before sunset as the afternoon prayer; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن جرير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله { وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها }

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses the night times and ends of the day as morning and evening; al-Tabataba’i says this supports his earlier explanation.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار } قال بالغداة والعشي

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Kafi reports from Zarara that Abu Ja‘far interpreted the day’s ends as voluntary daytime prayer; al-Tabataba’i says this assumes tasbih means prayer generally or tasbih generally.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن زراره عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال قلت له { وأطراف النهار لعلك ترضى }؟

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Qummi reports from Abu ‘Abd Allah that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet sat upright before speaking; the excerpt ends before his words are given.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ولا تمدن عينيك } الآية قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام لما نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ‘made’ means created, with every living thing as its object: water has a full role in the existence of living beings.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن الجعل بمعنى الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage parallels the statement that God created every animal from water; its context of perceptible signs may exclude angels and beings like them, and modern science clarifies life’s connection with water.
rows.anchor: ولعل ورود القول في سياق تعداد الآيات المحسوسة يوجب انصراف الحكم

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majma‘ defines rawasi as firmly settled mountains, mayd as motion in different directions, and fijaj as wide paths between two mountains.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع الرواسي الجبال رست ترسو رسوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God set firm mountains in the earth to keep it from swaying and made broad routes through them so people could reach their destinations and homes.
rows.anchor: وجعلنا في تلك الجبال طرقا واسعة هي سبل لعلهم يهتدون منها إلى مقاصدهم ومواطنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates a special relation between mountains and earthquakes: without mountains, the earth’s crust would be agitated.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن للجبال ارتباطا خاصا بالزلازل ولولاها لاضطربت الأرض بقشرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protected sky most likely means protection from devils, as in the statement that God guarded it from every accursed devil.
rows.anchor: كأن المراد بكون السماء محفوظة حفظها من الشياطين كما قال وحفظناها من كل شيطان رجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky’s signs are its changing celestial events, which point to unified governance resting on one creator.
rows.anchor: والمراد بآيات السماء الحوادث المختلفة السماوية التي تدل على وحدة التدبير واستناده إلى موجدها الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse assigns an orbit to night, day, sun, and moon: night is the conical shadow alongside earth opposite the sun, day is its opposite, and each has its own course.
rows.anchor: الآية ظاهرة في إثبات الفلك لكل من الليل وهو الظل المخروطي الملازم لوجه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are conditions relative to earth and its atmosphere; the sun and fixed stars shine intrinsically, while the moon and planets reflect light, and their day-night conditions differ from ours.
rows.anchor: والمراد مع ذلك بيان الأوضاع والأحوال الحادثة بالنسبة إلى الأرض وفي جوها وإن كانت حال الأجرام الأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabaha here means moving through water by cleaving it; the plural verb treats the celestial bodies as rational agents, as in other Qur’anic usage.
rows.anchor: وقوله { يسبحون } من السبح بمعنى الجري في الماء بخرقه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines naks as turning a thing upside down, as in a child born feet first; the verse’s phrase depicts the people reversing truth and falsehood.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب النكس قلب الشيء على رأسه ومنه نكس الولد إذا خرج رجله قبل رأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They put the false charge that Abraham was the wrongdoer above the truth that they were wrongdoers; they use their knowledge that idols cannot speak to convict him of smashing them.
rows.anchor: كناية أو استعارة بالكناية عن قلبهم الباطل على مكان الحق الذي ظهر لهم والحق على مكان الباطل

words: أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham does not defend himself; he turns their admission that idols cannot speak into a proof that they know and can do nothing, can neither benefit nor harm, and therefore are unworthy of worship.
rows.anchor: لازم كونهم لا ينطقون أن لا يعلموا شيئا ولا يقدروا على شيء، ولازم ذلك أن لا ينفعوكم شيئا

words: مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is pointless when its objects can neither benefit nor harm, since worship is undertaken either in hope of good or in fear of harm.
rows.anchor: أن يكون عبادتهم لغوا إذ العبادة إما لرجاء خير أو لخوف شر وليس عندهم شيء من ذلك

words: أُفٍّۢ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Uff to you’ expresses rebuke and disavowal of them and their gods after their divinity has been disproved.
rows.anchor: تزجر وتبر منهم ومن آلهتهم بعد إبطال ألوهيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s rebuke for lack of reason follows his earlier testimony to divine unity after establishing it.
rows.anchor: وهذا كشهادته على وحدانيته تعالى بعد إثباتها في قوله فيما مر { وأنا على ذلكم من الشاهدين } ،

words: حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Abraham had already disproved the idols, his silence let them treat the hinted smashing as a proven crime; they call burning him defense of their gods, and ‘if you will act’ is incitement.
rows.anchor: وبهذا المقدار من السكوت وعدم الرد قضوا عليه بثبوت الجرم وأن جزاءه أن يحرق بالنار

words: يَٰنَارُ كُونِى بَرْدًۭا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s creative command changed the fire’s heat, burning, and destructive properties into coolness and safety for Abraham, a miraculous breach of ordinary causal patterns.
rows.anchor: خطاب تكويني للنار تبدلت به خاصة حرارتها وإحراقها وإفنائها بردا وسلاما بالنسبة إلى إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational inquiry tracks repeated events with known causal links, so it cannot detail unexplained miracles; spiritual powers have some role, discussed in volume one’s treatment of miracles.
rows.anchor: وأما الخوارق التي نجهل الروابط فيها فلا مجرى لها فيها. نعم نعلم إجمالا أن لهمم النفوس دخلا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine ‘command’ means real, inward effusions and stations that believers attain through good deeds as divine mercy; the Imam guides people through this command.
rows.anchor: فهو الفيوضات المعنوية والمقامات الباطنية التي يهتدي إليها المؤمنون بأعمالهم الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi in ‘by Our command’ can mark cause or instrument; the Imam first possesses the command and then conveys its inward gifts to people according to their ranks.
rows.anchor: فهو متلبس به أولا ومنه ينتشر في الناس على اختلاف مقاماتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam links people and God in inward spiritual gifts, while the Prophet links them in outward divine law; the Imam guides souls to their stations and the Prophet to true beliefs and good deeds.
rows.anchor: كما أن النبي رابط بين الناس وبين ربهم في أخذ الفيوضات الظاهرية وهي الشرائع الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophethood and imamate can be combined in one person, as with Abraham and his two sons.
rows.anchor: وربما تجتمع النبوة والإمامة كما في إبراهيم وابنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary points ahead to Job’s story in Sad, back to Idris in Maryam, ahead to Ishmael in al-Saffat, and ahead to Dhu al-Kifl in Sad.
rows.anchor: وستجيء قصة أيوب عليه السلام في سورة ص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nun is Jonah son of Matta, the prophet associated with the whale and sent to Nineveh; after his people repented and believed as punishment approached, God lifted it, Jonah departed, and the whale swallowed him before God rescued and sent him back.
rows.anchor: النون الحوت وذو النون هو يونس النبي ابن متى صاحب الحوت الذي بعث إلى أهل نينوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah left angry at his people because they had not believed in him.
rows.anchor: أي واذكر ذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا أي لقومه حيث لم يؤمنوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean that Jonah thought God would not constrict him, using qadara in the sense of constricting as in ‘restricted his provision.’
rows.anchor: أي لن نضيق عليه من قدر عليه رزقه أي ضاق كما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The departure may be a figurative depiction: Jonah acted as one angry with his master and imagining he could escape the master’s reach, without literally intending that meaning.
rows.anchor: واردا مورد التمثيل أي كان ذهابه هذا ومفارقة قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A literal claim that Jonah was angry with God or thought God could not overpower him is incompatible with the dignity and divinely protected infallibility of prophets.
rows.anchor: وأما كونه عليه السلام مغاضبا لربه حقيقة وظنه أن الله لا يقدر عليه جدا فمما يجل ساحة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis: God tested Jonah through the whale, it swallowed him, and he called to his Lord from inside it.
rows.anchor: فيه إيجاز بالحذف والكلام متفرع عليه والتقدير فابتلاه الله بالحوت فالتقمه فنادى في بطنه ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘darknesses’ most likely mean the darkness of night, the sea, and the whale’s belly, an explanation also reported from others.
rows.anchor: ظلمة البحر وظلمة بطن الحوت وظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah disavows what his departure could imply: that there was any refuge besides God, that God could object to him, or that anything might escape God’s power.
rows.anchor: فتبرأ من ذلك بقوله لا إله ألا أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah admits wrongdoing because his act represented injustice, though it was not intrinsically wrong and he did not intend sin; God disciplined him to purify his will for closeness.
rows.anchor: اعتراف بالظلم من حيث إنه أتى بعمل كان يمثل الظلم وإن لم يكن ظلما في نفسه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: A report attributed to Abu Ja‘far explains the judgment: the vineyard goes to its owner while the flock’s owner tends it until the vines recover, then each returns the other’s property.
rows.anchor: قال تدفع الكرم إلى صاحب الغنم فيقوم عليه حتى يعود كما كان وتدفع الغنم إلى صاحب الكرم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The same vineyard-and-flock judgment is also narrated from Abu ‘Abd Allah.
rows.anchor: قال تدفع الكرم إلى صاحب الغنم فيقوم عليه حتى يعود كما كان وتدفع الغنم إلى صاحب الكرم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Reports through Sunni sources from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mas‘ud also identify the cultivated land in the case as a vineyard.
rows.anchor: وروي كون الحرث كرما من طرق أهل السنة عن عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
rows.claim: Other reports from the Imams of the Prophet’s family have meanings close to the judgment account; the author says his preceding explanation suffices to clarify them.
rows.anchor: وما مر في بيان معنى الآية يكفي في توضيح مضامين الروايات

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi says Solomon’s stormy wind came from every direction and went to the blessed land, meaning Jerusalem and Syria.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي وقوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Qummi transmits from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr and others, from Abu ‘Abd Allah, that God restored Job’s family from before the affliction and revived those who died during it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: In the Abu al-Jarud report, Abu Ja‘far says Jonah left in anger over his people’s deeds and thought God would not punish him for what he had done.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو الجارود
rows.claim: Abu al-Jarud’s report glosses the phrase as Jonah thinking that God would not punish him for his deed.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: In al-Rida’s debate with al-Ma’mun on prophetic infallibility, he says zan means Jonah was certain God would not constrict his provision, not that God lacked power; such a belief would be unbelief.
rows.anchor: وفي العيون بإسناده عن أبي الصلت الهروي في حديث الرضا عليه السلام مع المأمون

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Rida supports the meaning ‘constrict’ by citing the phrase about God restricting a person’s provision.
rows.anchor: ألا تسمع قول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Tahdhib reports from Abu ‘Abd Allah a set of four prayers for four needs; the Jonah prayer is for grief and anxiety, answered by God’s rescue from distress and promise to rescue believers.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال أربع لأربع

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Khisal also transmits this meaning from the Prophet in an unlinked report (mursal).
rows.anchor: أقول وروى هذا المعنى في الخصال عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم مرسلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zabur most likely means David’s scripture, which God names as a Zabur elsewhere; proposals that it means the Qur’an or revealed books generally, including those after Moses, lack evidence.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بالزبور كتاب داود عليه السلام وقد سمي بهذا الاسم في قوله وآتينا داود زبورا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says al-Zabur means the Qur’an or all revealed books, or books revealed to prophets after Moses; the author finds no evidence for these readings.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به القرآن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the dhikr as the Torah, which this sura calls ‘reminder’ in two places.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالذكر قيل هو التوراة وقد سماها الله به في موضعين من هذه السورة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes dhikr as the Qur’an, which God calls a reminder in several passages; on this reading, ‘after’ marks rank rather than chronology.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو القرآن وقد سماه الله ذكرا في مواضع من كلامه وكون الزبور بعد الذكر على هذا القول بعدية رتبية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view identifies dhikr as the Preserved Tablet; the author dismisses it as untenable.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو اللوح المحفوظ وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance means property passing to someone without a transaction; here it is transfer of authority over earth’s benefits and the establishment of life’s blessings among the inheritors.
rows.anchor: والمراد من وراثة الأرض انتقال التسلط على منافعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly inheritance means the earth is cleansed of idolatry and disobedience and inhabited by a righteous society worshiping God alone, as in the promise of succession to believers.
rows.anchor: كالتمتع الصالح بأمتعتها وزيناتها فيكون مؤدى الآية أن الأرض ستتطهر من الشرك والمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly reading connects the verse’s inheritance with God’s promise that believers will succeed to the earth and worship without associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: كما يشير إليه قوله تعالى وعد الله الذين آمنوا منكم وعملوا الصالحات ليستخلفنهم في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Otherworldly inheritance means stations of nearness gained in earthly life, which become the bliss of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وإما أخروية وهي مقامات القرب التي اكتسبوها في حياتهم الدنيا فإنها من بركات الحياة الأرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife reading is supported by the saved people saying they inherited the earth in Paradise and by the description of believers as inheritors of Paradise.
rows.anchor: كما يشير إليه قوله تعالى حكاية عن أهل الجنة وقالوا الحمد لله الذي أورثنا الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is unrestricted and includes both worldly and otherworldly inheritance; neither sense should be made exclusive.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن الآية مطلقة ولا موجب لتخصيصها بإحدى الوراثتين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some restrict inheritance to the afterlife, arguing from the preceding verse’s mention of resurrection that no earth remains afterward for the righteous to inherit.
rows.anchor: فهم بين من يخصها بالوراثة الأخروية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the afterlife-only argument: attachment to the preceding verse is not required, since this verse may attach to the earlier statement about believers who do righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: فمن الممكن أن تكون معطوفة على قوله السابق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Others restrict inheritance to worldly rule at the rise of Islam or the appearance of the Mahdi, citing relevant verses and widely transmitted reports through both Sunni and Shi‘i routes.
rows.anchor: وبين من يخصها بالوراثة الدنيوية ويحملها على زمان ظهور الإسلام أو ظهور المهدي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context links this verse to the earlier account of believers’ recompense: the previous passage details their afterlife reward, while this one details worldly recompense through inheriting the earth.
rows.anchor: الاعتبار بالسياق أن تكون معطوفة على قوله السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humankind was commanded to one religion but split: the differing afterlife recompense favors believers, while the earthly recompense grants inheritance to the righteous rather than others.
rows.anchor: أنا أمرناهم بدين واحد لكنهم تقطعوا واختلفوا فاختلف مجازاتنا لهم أما في الآخرة فللمؤمنين سعي مشكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfillment of vows means completing what became incumbent through a vow or a similar undertaking.
rows.anchor: إتمام ما لزمهم بنذر أو نحوه

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
rows.claim: The Imams of the Prophet’s family interpret this as the women’s tawaf: after leaving ihram, all its prohibitions lift except those involving women, which lift with this final rite.
rows.anchor: طواف النساء على ما في تفسير أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام فإن الخروج من الإحرام يحلل له كل ما حرم به إلا النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ancient House is the Ka‘ba; it is called ancient because of its age and was the first house built for God’s worship, as in the verse about the house at Bakkah.
rows.anchor: والبيت العتيق هو الكعبة المشرفة سميت به لقدمه فإنه أول بيت بني لعبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ka‘ba had stood for roughly four thousand years at the commentary’s present and for more than 2,500 years when these verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى على هذا البيت اليوم زهاء أربعة آلاف سنة وهو معمور وكان له يوم نزول الآيات أكثر من ألفين وخمسمائة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hurma is what may not be violated and must be observed; awthan are idols, and zawr is deviation from truth, hence lying or false speech.
rows.anchor: الحرمة ما لا يجوز انتهاكه ووجب رعايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ summarizes the rites legislated for Abraham and later pilgrims: ihram, circumambulation, prayer, sacrifice sincerely for God, and avoidance of associating partners.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر ذلك أي الذي شرعناه لإبراهيم عليه السلام ومن بعده من نسك الحج هو ذلك الذي ذكرناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exalting God’s inviolable limits means refraining from crossing the boundaries He set and committing what lies beyond them.
rows.anchor: وهي الأمور التي نهى عنها وضرب دونها حدودا منع عن تعديها واقتراف ما وراءها وتعظيمها الكف عن التجاوز إليها

words: وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمُ إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sanctities sentence prepares for the permission of livestock with exceptions: although livestock are lawful provisions, the exception indicates that some carry a divine prohibition.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الجملة توطئة وتمهيد لما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What is recited to you’ refers to prohibitions already being recited, not a future reference to the verse in al-Ma’idah; food prohibitions appeared in al-An‘am, al-Nahl, and al-Baqara, so a future reading is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: استمرار التلاوة، فإن محرمات الأكل نزلت في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though carrion, blood, pork, and meat dedicated to other than God are all forbidden, the pilgrimage context especially targets pagan offerings to idols at the Ka‘ba, Safa, Marwa, and Mina.
rows.anchor: إلا أن العناية في الآية بشهادة سياق ما قبلها وما بعدها بخصوص ما أهل به لغير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands generally prohibit approaching idols and false speech used for idol worship in pilgrimage, including naming idols over sacrificial animals; the following fa makes this a consequence of the prior command to honor sanctities.
rows.anchor: نهي عام عن التقرب إلى الأصنام وقول الباطل أورد لغرض التقرب إلى الأصنام في عمل الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the idols defilement signals the reason to avoid them; applying avoidance directly to the objects, rather than acts involving them, emphatically extends the prohibition.
rows.anchor: إشعار بالعلية كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is explanatory: it identifies the defilement as idols; reading it as source or partitive, so that it means idol worship, strains and disrupts the straightforward sense.
rows.anchor: بيانية، وذكر بعضهم أنها ابتدائية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take min as indicating origin: avoid the defilement that comes from idols, namely their worship; another group reads it partitivally as a defiling aspect of idols, namely worship. The author calls both readings strained.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنها ابتدائية والمعنى اجتنبوا الرجس الكائن من الأوثان وهو عبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanif, plural hunafa’, means turning from the extremes toward the center; being hanif for God means turning from all other gods to Him, matching the meaning of not associating partners.
rows.anchor: وهو المائل من الأطراف إلى حاق الوسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Hanifs for God’ and ‘not associating with Him’ are both circumstantial clauses describing those commanded to avoid idols and dedicate sacrifices to God; pagans’ pilgrimage chant contradicted this.
rows.anchor: حال كونكم مائلين إليه ممن سواه غير مشركين به

words: فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتَخْطَفُهُ ٱلطَّيْرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolater falls from humanity’s highest station into misguidance’s abyss and is seized by Satan as if snatched by birds; the wind carrying him far away is a second simile emphasizing distance.
rows.anchor: شبه المشرك في شركه وسقوطه به من أعلى درجات الإنسانية إلى هاوية الضلال فيصيده الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sha‘ira means a sign; God’s sha‘a’ir are markers He established for obedience, including Safa and Marwa and sacrificial camels.
rows.anchor: الأعلام التي نصبها الله تعالى لطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ predicates an omitted subject: ‘the matter is as stated’; the following clause identifies honoring God’s signs with piety of the hearts.
rows.anchor: خبر لمبتدأ محذوف أي الأمر ذلك الذي قلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan sura calls people to believe in God and the Last Day, contrasts believers’ fine servitude with disbelievers’ vices, then gives glad tidings and warnings including the annihilation of denying peoples from Noah through Jesus.
rows.anchor: دعوة إلى الإيمان بالله واليوم الآخر وتمييز المؤمنين من الكفار بذكر ما لهؤلاء من جميل صفات العبودية

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says falh means a cleft or splitting, illustrated by iron splitting iron; falah then means success and attainment of a goal.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الفلح - بالفتح فالسكون - الشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success has worldly and afterlife forms: worldly happiness includes long life, wealth, and honor; the afterlife brings permanence, freedom from poverty, freedom from disgrace, and knowledge without ignorance.
rows.anchor: فالدنيوي الظفر بالسعادات التي تطيب بها الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling attainment falah evokes splitting through the obstacle and uncovering the face of one’s desired goal.
rows.anchor: فتسمية الظفر بالسعادة فلاحا بعناية أن فيه شقا للمانع وكشفا عن وجه المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iman is affirming something while committing to its implications; Qur’anic faith in God affirms His oneness, messengers, the Last Day, and their message, with general obedience.
rows.anchor: والإيمان هو الإذعان والتصديق بشيء بالالتزام بلوازمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an regularly pairs believers’ praise and reward with righteous action, as in its promise of a good life to anyone who acts righteously while believing and its praise of believers who do good works.
rows.anchor: ولذا نجد القرآن كلما ذكر المؤمنين بوصف جميل أو أجر جزيل شفع الإيمان بالعمل الصالح كقوله من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief is not mere mental assent without commitment: faith includes settled assurance and adherence to implications, whereas knowledge can coexist with failure to abandon harmful or shameful habits.
rows.anchor: وليس مجرد الاعتقاد بشيء إيمانا به حتى مع عدم الالتزام بلوازمه وآثاره فإن الإيمان علم بالشيء مع السكون والاطمئنان إليه
